technologies: Cloudflare Workers platform and current limits
baseline.versionPolicy: Outcome requirements are stable; recheck limits, bindings, consistency, delivery, compatibility, and lifecycle semantics against current official Cloudflare documentation and pinned tooling.

owns: Cloudflare resource and external protocol adaptation
independently deployable message and service schemas

hardOutcomes: Cross-service dependencies and synchronous calls cannot form unsafe cycles.
Each authoritative business fact has one logical writer or an explicit conflict protocol.
Platform bindings remain at declared edges and do not leak into a declared pure core.

invariants.outcome: Each deployed service owns its business rules and authoritative data, and static dependencies, synchronous calls, contracts, and cross-service writes cannot bypass ownership or form unsafe cycles.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Any monorepo topology qualifies when deployment boundaries, dependency evidence, contract windows, and write paths prove the same independent ownership and termination properties.

invariants.outcome: Request-local state, post-response work, and every adopted Cloudflare resource follow their real execution-lifetime, consistency, delivery, retry, ordering, eviction, and transaction semantics.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Different resources or coordination protocols comply when fault tests prove required durability, conflict behavior, safe duplicates, and bounded post-response work.

invariants.outcome: Tenant identity is derived from trusted context and enforced without bypass across authorization, storage keys, caches, queues, logs, and every resource binding.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Shared or isolated resources comply when cross-tenant negative tests prove an untrusted tenant identifier cannot read, mutate, infer, or route another tenant's data.

invariants.outcome: Every adopted public, service, message, and static-asset boundary validates untrusted input, enforces resource authorization and least privilege, and cannot bypass an owning Worker's protection path.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Different routers, schemas, service contracts, or asset delivery modes comply when negative tests prove hostile input and protected assets cannot escape validation, authorization, or the owning Worker boundary.

invariants.outcome: Each environment's effective bindings, resource instances, migrations, routes, compatibility settings, and secret injection are explicit, isolated, reproducible, and non-disclosing.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Dashboard, configuration-as-code, or another source qualifies when the effective deployed state is reviewable, reproducible, environment-isolated, and keeps secrets out of artifacts and logs.

invariants.outcome: Every supported deployment unit can resolve configuration, type-check, test, build, and prepare the intended target environment from locked dependencies and a clean checkout.
invariants.equivalenceCriteria: Any task runner and package topology comply when repository commands select the real affected deployment units and produce reviewable artifacts without undeclared dashboard or machine state.

proves: Wrangler resolves the selected deployment unit and can prepare its upload artifact.
doesNotProve: Remote environment bindings, secrets, migrations, routes, static-asset authorization, or runtime behavior are correct.

proves: Repository-selected tests pass for exercised worker and resource semantics.
doesNotProve: Unexercised production limits, version skew, delivery schedules, or tenant attacks are safe.

proves: The repository-selected type check passes across declared source and contract references.
doesNotProve: Runtime binding behavior, authorization, or distributed consistency is correct.

scenarios.failure: A Durable Object is evicted or restarted while authoritative facts exist only in memory, or a read-modify-write crosses non-storage I/O without conflict control.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Recreate the object around adversarial I/O timing and prove durable facts recover and conflicting writes use a transaction, convergent synchronous section, or optimistic control.

scenarios.failure: A response returns while a floating Promise still owns a required side effect, or waitUntil starts unbounded, unobserved work that outlives the invocation contract.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Exercise response completion with pending effects; prove each effect is awaited or owned by bounded and observable waitUntil, consumer, workflow, or scheduled execution, and request-scoped resources never leak across invocations.

scenarios.failure: A queue message is delivered again or out of order after a partial side effect, producing duplicate billing, entitlement, notification, or mutation.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Replay duplicates and reorder dependent messages while injecting acknowledgement failures; prove idempotency, deduplication, conflict handling, and dead-letter recovery.

scenarios.failure: Static Assets serves protected or tenant-specific content before the Worker can authenticate and authorize the request.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Probe protected asset paths with missing, invalid, and cross-tenant identity; prove run_worker_first or an equivalent asset boundary routes every protected request through authorization.

scenarios.failure: An attacker changes a tenant identifier or cache, queue, storage, or service key and reaches another tenant's data or effects.
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Exercise cross-tenant reads, writes, enumeration, cache reuse, queued work, logs, and direct service calls using trusted and attacker-controlled identity inputs.
